independent_tui_product_decisions.recorded_in: architecture-reset.md and decisions.md D-08 through D-109
independent_tui_product_decisions.package_boundary: friday-tui independently installable; no imports or dependency on friday-chat, friday-cli or any CLI code; UI-neutral Friday runtime packages allowed
independent_tui_product_decisions.busy_slash_quit: Normal command when idle; busy submit rejected and editor text retained; Ctrl+Q/Quit action request safe exit
independent_tui_product_decisions.command_parity: Equivalent syntax, aliases, effects, errors and state; TUI-specific result presentation permitted; ongoing parity as Chat commands evolve; TUI-only additions permitted
independent_tui_product_decisions.config_chooser: D-13/D-48: when --config is absent, show an existing-file chooser initially listing runtime-config candidates from the captured launch working directory, with browsing to another path; no automatic user-directory or recursive search. Explicit --config bypasses the list. D-55 selects shallow content inspection; exact key signature remains open.
independent_tui_product_decisions.chooser_browse_path_entry: D-58: Browse supports folder navigation and typed/pasted absolute, relative and ~ home paths to existing runtime config files. Relative input resolves from the displayed Browse folder, initially the launch working directory. Missing or invalid choices retain in-chooser D-50 recovery; no automatic search, file creation or change to explicit --config.
independent_tui_product_decisions.chooser_refresh: D-59: provide a visible keyboard-focusable Refresh action that rescans only the captured launch folder's runtime candidates on demand. Added, removed and newly recognizable files update the list; no watcher or automatic list update, wider search, full validation or runtime start. Retry of a selected path rereads that path independently.
independent_tui_product_decisions.chooser_symlinks: D-60: include direct-child .yaml/.yml links in initial and refreshed candidate lists when they resolve to readable regular runtime-shaped files, including outside-folder targets. Exclude broken, cyclic, unreadable, directory-target and non-runtime links from automatic listing; Browse and D-50 recovery remain. No recursive search or full validation during listing.
independent_tui_product_decisions.chooser_candidate_filter: D-49/D-55/D-57: shallow, read-only top-level YAML inspection finds likely Friday Chat runtime files including custom names and incomplete but recognizable files, while recognized model-library and CLI presentation YAML are excluded. Unrecognized files remain reachable through Browse. Listing does not resolve credentials, follow service references, fully validate or start services. Exact keys and filesystem edge rules remain bootstrap-contract work.
independent_tui_product_decisions.chooser_invalid_selection: D-50: keep the chooser open with an actionable validation error and Retry of the selected path, Browse to another file and Quit. Retry rereads the selected path; an invalid file cannot start the runtime.
independent_tui_product_decisions.explicit_config_invalid: D-51: an invalid explicit --config file reports a configuration error and exits nonzero without opening the chooser or starting the runtime. This preserves the current Chat error direction without a Chat code dependency. Real-provider startup failure remains separate.
independent_tui_product_decisions.chooser_empty_list: D-52/D-59: if the captured launch folder has no likely runtime-config candidates, keep the chooser open with a clear empty-list message and Refresh, Browse and Quit. Do not automatically search elsewhere, create a file or start the runtime.
independent_tui_product_decisions.chooser_real_start_failure: D-53: after a valid chooser selection, clean up partially started real-runtime services on startup failure, show the error and return to the chooser with Retry of the selected file, Browse and Quit when cleanup succeeds. Do not silently use fake. D-56 governs failed cleanup.
independent_tui_product_decisions.explicit_config_real_start_failure: D-54: after valid explicit --config, failed real-runtime startup closes partial services, reports startup and any cleanup failure, and exits nonzero without opening the chooser or falling back to fake.
independent_tui_product_decisions.chooser_start_cleanup_both_fail: D-56: if real startup and cleanup both fail after chooser selection, report both failures, restore the terminal as far as possible and exit nonzero without in-process Retry or Browse.
independent_tui_product_decisions.linux_verification: Automated checks during construction; hands-on Linux terminal UAT required before first-release acceptance

independent_tui_product_decisions.display_clear: D-33: /cls and /clearscreen clear the displayed conversation, pinned prompt and Activity view without replacement text. The pin remains empty until the next accepted conversational prompt; session history, memory and persisted transcripts are unchanged. D-105 keeps separate failed-prompt editor recovery and its Restore action through this display clear.
independent_tui_product_decisions.transcript_session_scope: D-34: first release shows the current transcript session and retains /sessions and /transcript inspection/export behavior, but has no control for switching active transcript sessions. /switch [agent] changes the active agent.
independent_tui_product_decisions.selected_text_copy: D-35: selected visible Activity and shown provider reasoning can be copied. Copy includes only rendered text; oversized tool arguments contribute their preview and truncation notice, never discarded overflow, and hidden reasoning is unavailable. Copy does not add these views to transcripts or exports.
independent_tui_product_decisions.history_navigation: D-36: pause following whenever away from bottom; keep the latest pin while reading its response but hide it in older exchanges. Show a visible clickable and keyboard-focusable Jump to latest control away from the bottom; activation or scrolling to the bottom restores the pin when available and resumes following new output.
independent_tui_product_decisions.rendered_history_eviction: D-37: show a notice when older conversation messages leave the bounded view. Direct to /transcript only for saved messages and say when no saved transcript is available. No first-release Load older control or claim that transient Activity/reasoning is recoverable from transcripts.
independent_tui_product_decisions.editor_key_behavior: D-38: in the TUI editor, Enter submits once and Ctrl+Enter inserts a newline without submitting when the terminal distinguishes those keys. Multiline paste never submits. Keep focusable Submit and Insert newline actions; check physical macOS/Linux terminal key delivery and document the fallback where Ctrl+Enter is indistinguishable. No Chat or friday-cli behavior change.
independent_tui_product_decisions.newline_fallback: D-39: where Ctrl+Enter is indistinguishable from Enter, use the visible clickable and keyboard-focusable Insert newline control; do not assign a second default newline shortcut in the first release. Verify physical terminal behavior and document the fallback.
independent_tui_product_decisions.command_palette_selection: D-40: choosing a slash command from the palette fills and focuses the prompt editor for review and arguments; selection alone does not dispatch or cause command side effects. Enter or Submit later invokes normal admission once.
independent_tui_product_decisions.slash_command_suggestions: D-66: typing a leading slash command automatically shows name and alias matches from the TUI's active registry as the name changes. Display alone leaves the draft untouched, does not dispatch, and does not change Enter submission. Help and palette remain available; D-67 settles inline selection behavior and D-68 settles keyboard controls.
independent_tui_product_decisions.slash_suggestion_selection: D-67: choosing an inline suggestion completes its name or alias token in the current editor draft, preserving following arguments and editor focus. It never dispatches; Enter or Submit later invokes normal admission. D-68 uses Up/Down highlighting and Tab insertion while open, with Tab focus navigation when closed; Enter always submits. Pointer/dismissal details remain technical UI work; palette whole-draft replacement remains D-41.
independent_tui_product_decisions.slash_subcommand_suggestions: D-69: after a recognized slash command and space, suggest declared subcommands from active TUI registry metadata as their token is typed. Apply D-67/D-68 fill-only selection to that token; do not execute, suggest free-form values or query runtime services for matches. Commands without declared subcommands have no invented second-token list.
independent_tui_product_decisions.slash_usage_hints: D-70: show a short, display-only required/optional argument shape for a recognized slash command or subcommand from active TUI metadata. Update or clear the hint as recognized syntax changes. Do not fill values, dispatch or call the runtime; full purpose and examples remain in Help and palette.
independent_tui_product_decisions.editor_history: D-71/D-75: during a running TUI session, accepted conversational prompts, slash commands, @agent messages and enabled/admitted ! commands are recallable into the editor without execution. Disabled/rejected routes, unsent/busy-rejected drafts and output are not entries. D-72: editor recall is in-process only, discarded on exit and empty after restart, independent of /history, memory and transcripts. D-73: browsing preserves an unsent draft and editing position, restoring both when leaving without submission; browsed entries are editable copies. D-74: Up/Down at multiline editor caret boundaries traverse history when suggestions are closed; open slash suggestions take arrow priority. No F3/F4 history binding.
independent_tui_product_decisions.context_file_browser: D-76: first-release Context sidebar includes read-only folder browsing and file selection alongside current session, working directory, active agent and available services. Browsing does not ingest memory or edit files. D-77: deliberate pointer or keyboard selection immediately initiates attachment for the next eligible model turn without a separate Add action or prompt submission; focus movement and scrolling do not attach. Show loading, attached and failed status. D-78: attachment remains active across later accepted turns until visible keyboard-focusable Remove; removal affects future turns, not an already admitted turn, and does not edit file or memory. D-79: attachments are in-process only, discarded on exit and empty after relaunch, independent of transcripts. D-80: selecting a second distinct file adds it alongside the first; each has its own Remove action. D-81: capture content at selection and reuse across turns; reselecting the same file refreshes in place, while failed refresh keeps the last good snapshot with an error. D-82: first-release attachments extract real text/code/text-data, PDF, DOCX and XLSX content with installed readers, no placeholders or empty success. D-83: first-release scanned/image-only PDF attachment uses Tesseract OCR through a separate PDF page-rendering step; missing OCR/render support or empty recognized text is a visible failure. D-84: mixed PDF pages use embedded text where usable and Tesseract only where it is absent, preserving order and avoiding duplicate page text. D-85: Tesseract is a separately system-installed executable on macOS/Linux, not bundled or auto-installed by the TUI; missing OCR produces an actionable attachment error without blocking unrelated file types. D-86: failure of any required OCR page rejects the whole new PDF attachment with a page-specific error and no partial model input; failed refresh retains the last complete snapshot. D-87: OCR defaults to English and accepts one or more installed Tesseract language packs through a TUI-only setting in the shared presentation file; missing packs fail OCR attachment without silent fallback. D-88: a cross-platform PDF page renderer is declared as an installed TUI package dependency, with no separate user renderer install; Tesseract remains system-installed. D-89: XLSX attachment includes every worksheet, including hidden ones, labeled by sheet name in workbook order as one snapshot; the TUI must not silently use the existing active-sheet default. D-90: a failed worksheet read rejects the entire new workbook with the sheet and cause named, no partial model input, and last complete snapshot retained on failed refresh; other files remain attached. D-91: formula cells include the expression and any workbook-saved result with distinct sheet/cell labels; missing saved result is indicated without calculation. D-92: an individual file over the TUI extracted-content limit is rejected whole with a visible size error and no partial new model input; failed refresh preserves the last complete snapshot. D-93: a new file that would exceed the combined attachment budget is rejected without changing existing snapshots or evicting files; users remove files and retry, and an over-budget refresh keeps its old snapshot. D-94: optional TUI-only per-file and combined limit settings in the shared presentation file use typed defaults and validation; CLI/runtime behavior remains unchanged. D-95: both settings use estimated tokens of complete formatted attachment text, including labels and OCR/formula content; exact provider counts are not promised. D-96: omitted limits use fixed defaults across models/providers and do not scale with context-window metadata; valid explicit values override them, while runtime context budgeting remains separate. D-97: omitted defaults are 4,000 estimated tokens per file and 8,000 combined, with exactly-at-limit accepted and above-limit rejected; admission does not guarantee that an 8,192-token model turn fits. D-98/D-99: check the fully assembled first and later conversational provider requests; an overage may trigger one configured, eligible older-turn compaction attempt, followed by full reassembly and re-estimation. An initial step that remains over budget keeps the exact draft/caret and attachments without accepting a turn or invoking its primary provider/tool; a later step stops incomplete and retains prior tool activity/effects. Compaction may call its own model service and persist memory maintenance. Usable-text criteria, language-code validation bounds, exact renderer selection, estimator/headroom, field names, allowed override ranges remain open; D-100 separately settles recognized post-estimate provider context-length rejection and neutral runtime contracts are needed. No Chat/CLI dependency or existing package behavior change is authorized.
independent_tui_product_decisions.palette_draft_replacement: D-41: when an unsent draft is present, selecting a slash command from the palette asks before replacement. Cancel retains the draft exactly; confirm replaces it and focuses the editor without submitting. Empty editors fill directly.
independent_tui_product_decisions.activity_initial_visibility: D-42: open Activity automatically on its first entry without stealing editor focus or overriding paused conversation following; allow user collapse/reopen and retain later entries without forcing the view open again. Keep the collapsed control visible.
independent_tui_product_decisions.collapsed_activity_count: D-43: the collapsed Activity header shows newly appended entries since collapse; status updates to an existing entry do not increment it. Reopen or /cls /clearscreen resets the count; bounded eviction while collapsed gets a header indicator and detailed notice on reopen.
independent_tui_product_decisions.activity_scroll_return: D-44: expanded Activity follows new entries only at its own bottom. Scrolling up pauses; a clickable keyboard-focusable Jump to latest Activity control or scrolling back down resumes without moving the conversation or prompt pin. The conversation Jump to latest remains separate.
independent_tui_product_decisions.activity_placement: D-45: first-release Activity is inline within the conversation exchange or user-entered tool-command entry that produced it, before the final answer/result. It is collapsible and internally scrollable, including at narrow terminal sizes; no persistent Activity side pane.
independent_tui_product_decisions.older_activity_state: D-46: accepting a new conversational prompt leaves older inline Activity sections in each user's chosen expanded/collapsed state, subject to bounded retention and explicit clear. The new exchange's Activity opens independently on its first entry.
independent_tui_product_decisions.tui_runtime_default: D-47: interactive TUI startup with explicit or chosen config defaults to real provider-backed Friday runtime; --runtime fake is explicit. A failed real startup never silently falls back to fake. Existing friday-chat fake default and friday-cli behavior remain unchanged; version/startup replay precedence is separate.
independent_tui_product_decisions.tui_runtime_mode_environment: D-61: FRIDAY_CHAT_RUNTIME remains specific to the existing Chat launcher. TUI ignores it for mode selection and has no first-release runtime-mode environment override; omitted TUI --runtime means real and explicit --runtime fake means fake. Runtime YAML environment interpolation and credential lookup are unaffected; Chat's existing override remains unchanged.
independent_tui_product_decisions.startup_replay_result: D-62: after successful startup --replay FILE, keep a read-only file/processed-count result view until Quit. Preserve version-before-replay-before-configured-start precedence and isolated fake replay; no config chooser, prompt/command admission or automatic transition to a configured session. D-63 limits first-release replay data on the result screen to file and processed-turn count, without a browsable per-turn record. D-64 keeps a failed startup replay's read-only file/error view until Quit, then exits nonzero without chooser or interactive startup. D-65 excludes in-process Retry; correct the cause and relaunch. Neutral error and cleanup details remain technical directive work.
independent_tui_product_decisions.reasoning_display: First release: hidden by default; in-app toggle applies to subsequent provider reasoning events without config writes or retroactive hidden-text retention; no CLI or generation change
independent_tui_product_decisions.tool_activity: First release: bounded in-process, non-persisted/non-exported Activity for automatic, manual /run-tool, delegated-agent and workflow tool calls; show actor, actual execution arguments without credential masking up to a per-entry display limit, and status. Oversized values have a marked truncated preview with overflow discarded from TUI memory; tool input is unchanged. An actual model or user request rejected before invocation is Not run with reason; pre-request tool selection or budget exclusions create no Activity entry. Suppress automatic tool results; /run-tool retains its inline result.
independent_tui_product_decisions.neutral_service_extraction: Allowed where needed: move reusable non-UI operations from Chat into a UI-neutral Friday service used by separate Chat and TUI handlers; prove Chat and friday-cli behavior unchanged
independent_tui_product_decisions.quit_exception: Normal Quit remains safe-point cleanup. A separate confirmed emergency Force quit may leave operation or cleanup incomplete and must say so.
independent_tui_product_decisions.real_provider_uat: Required before first-release acceptance with an executing tool; select and record the provider before final UAT; no provider or credentials chosen yet
independent_tui_product_decisions.initial_turn_budget_preflight: D-98 as refined by D-99: after normal Friday context selection, the first-release TUI checks the fully assembled first conversational provider request against the selected model effective input budget through a UI-neutral enforceable outcome. An overage permits one eligible runtime-configured older-turn compaction attempt and full reassembly/re-estimation. If it still exceeds budget, report total/available/overage, preserve exact editor draft/caret and active attachment snapshots, and create no accepted turn, prompt pin, editor recall, new transcript/session turn, blocked primary provider call or user-turn tool effect. Maintenance model calls and persistent memory effects are separate and visible. No Chat/CLI change. Exact estimator/reserve remain open; D-100 governs recognized provider context-length rejection after a passing estimate.
independent_tui_product_decisions.context_overage_compaction: D-99: check initial and later agent-loop conversational model steps. When over budget, request at most one eligible older-turn compaction through a UI-neutral Friday service if memory.compaction.enabled is true, respecting configured availability, in-flight/cooldown and protected/minimum older-history gates. The service may call a separate maintenance model and persist turn summaries or other configured memory work; report progress/result/failure. Reassemble and re-estimate the whole pending request even if target_met. Continue automatically if it fits; otherwise do not send the blocked primary request or execute further tools. A failed initial step retains draft/caret/attachments without an accepted turn; a failed later step is incomplete with prior activity and tool effects retained and no incomplete-turn transcript entry under D-103. No active-loop or attachment truncation, new TUI compaction setting, Chat/CLI dependency or behavior change. Manual /compact parity is separate; bind neutral contract and exact estimator/reserve before construction.
independent_tui_product_decisions.post_estimate_provider_context_rejection: D-100: if a conversational request passed Friday budget estimation and the provider then reports a recognized context-length error, the first-release TUI displays that post-send error and leaves correction/retry to the user. No TUI-triggered compaction or automatic resend; existing Friday LLM transport retry policy and Chat/friday-cli behavior remain unchanged. Preserve the initial submitted draft/caret for correction without overwriting a newer unsent draft, and retain active attachment snapshots. On a later agent-loop step, mark the turn incomplete, retain recorded Activity and completed tool effects, and run no further loop step. Do not claim the provider was never called or reverse completed runtime effects. A UI-neutral classification must distinguish context length from other invalid requests; D-101 binds empty-editor automatic restoration versus a Restore action for a newer draft. D-102 excludes a failed initial attempt from persisted transcripts; D-103 excludes a later post-tool incomplete turn. Bind classification and provider detail before construction; D-104/D-105 fix Restore placement after notice eviction and display clear, while D-106 clears old recovery after a different successful conversational turn; D-107 presents multiple pending failures in one chooser; D-108 retains confirmed selected entries until conversational success or D-109 confirmed dismissal; finite recovery-state limits are construction details.
independent_tui_product_decisions.failed_prompt_editor_recovery: D-101: after an initial post-send provider context-length rejection, restore the exact submitted prompt text and caret into an empty editor automatically, without submission or attachment changes. If a newer unsent draft is present, leave its text/caret/focus unchanged and show a visible pointer- and keyboard-activatable Restore failed prompt action with the provider-error notice. Activating Restore on a nonempty editor uses the existing D-41 Confirm/Cancel replacement pattern; Cancel preserves the newer draft, Confirm fills the editor with the failed prompt without sending it. No TUI compaction or resend. D-102 excludes failed-initial transcript persistence. D-104/D-105 keep the action beside the editor after error-notice eviction or display clearing; D-106 clears old recovery after a different successful conversational turn; D-107 presents multiple pending failures in one chooser; D-108 retains confirmed selected entries until conversational success or D-109 confirmed dismissal; finite recovery-state limits are construction details; Chat/friday-cli behavior is unchanged.
independent_tui_product_decisions.failed_initial_transcript: D-102: a first conversational request rejected by the provider for context length after a passing Friday estimate creates no persisted failed-attempt transcript entry. The provider-error notice and submitted prompt remain recoverable only during the current TUI run through D-101; relaunch does not reconstruct them from transcript data. A corrected successful resubmission is a distinct attempt recorded once through normal transcript persistence. This does not erase provider telemetry, compaction memory effects or existing transcript entries, while D-103 separately excludes a later post-tool incomplete-turn transcript entry. Bind neutral failure/persistence ordering before construction; Chat/friday-cli behavior is unchanged.
independent_tui_product_decisions.failed_later_turn_transcript: D-103: if a later agent-loop model step fails for context length after one or more tools execute, whether local overage after D-99 recovery or provider rejection under D-100, stop additional model/tool steps and show an incomplete turn with prior Activity only in the current bounded TUI view. Do not write an incomplete-turn transcript record, including prompt/status-only or serialized Activity. Prior completed transcript entries remain unchanged; executed tool effects, provider telemetry and compaction memory effects are not rolled back. Relaunch does not recover the incomplete turn or Activity from /transcript. Bind neutral failure/persistence ordering and test both paths with a fake executing tool and disposable transcript store; Chat/friday-cli behavior remains unchanged.
independent_tui_product_decisions.failed_prompt_restore_location: D-104: when a failed initial provider context-length error notice is evicted from the bounded conversation, keep a compact Restore failed prompt action beside the editor while that prompt remains recoverable in the current TUI run. The action is pointer- and keyboard-accessible, appears without focus theft and is absent when no failed prompt is recoverable. With a newer draft, D-41/D-101 Confirm/Cancel protects its text/caret; Confirm restores the exact failed prompt/caret without submission or another provider call. No Context-sidebar or transcript dependency; D-102 ends recovery on exit. Test eviction, narrow/reshaped layouts, focus, replacement and installed macOS/Linux UAT. D-105 also keeps editor recovery after an explicit /cls or /clearscreen display clear.
independent_tui_product_decisions.failed_prompt_display_clear_recovery: D-105: /cls and /clearscreen, and a shortcut invoking the same display clear, remove the conversation error notice, latest prompt pin and Activity under D-33 but keep a recoverable failed initial prompt and its labeled Restore action beside the editor during the current TUI run. Restore remains keyboard/pointer accessible without focus theft, follows D-41/D-101 Confirm/Cancel for an occupied editor and never resubmits automatically. D-102 excludes the failed attempt from persisted transcripts and ends recovery on exit. Test aliases/shortcut, view clearing, retained recovery, no new provider or transcript entry and installed macOS/Linux UAT. D-106 clears older recovery after a different successful conversational turn; D-107 presents multiple pending failures in one chooser; D-108 retains confirmed selected entries until conversational success or D-109 confirmed dismissal; finite recovery-state limits are construction details.
independent_tui_product_decisions.failed_prompt_successful_turn_cleanup: D-106: if an earlier failed initial provider-context prompt remains recoverable, submitting a different conversational prompt does not clear it at admission or during partial output. A successful completed-turn outcome clears the old recovery payload and removes Restore actions from beside the editor and any retained error notice; old error text may remain only as non-actionable bounded current-run display. A failed newer turn or slash command does not by itself clear the old recovery. D-102 continues to exclude the failed attempt from persistent transcripts; normal success persistence records the newer turn once. Test pending, partial, failed and successful outcomes with fake provider/disposable transcript, both action placements, no extra provider call, installed macOS/Linux UAT and unchanged Chat/friday-cli behavior. D-107 presents multiple pending failures in one chooser; D-108 retains confirmed selected entries until conversational success or D-109 confirmed dismissal; finite recovery-state limits are construction details.
independent_tui_product_decisions.multiple_failed_prompt_restore_chooser: D-107: if two or more initial provider-context prompts remain recoverable in one TUI run, show one editor-adjacent Restore failed prompts (N) control with an accurate count. It opens a keyboard/pointer chooser with distinct pending prompts newest first, with no separate Restore controls on retained error notices in this multiple-prompt state; one pending prompt uses singular Restore failed prompt and zero shows none. Opening, browsing and canceling preserve the editor draft/caret; selecting a prompt uses D-41/D-101 Confirm/Cancel before replacing a nonempty editor, with no automatic provider call. D-104/D-105 keep entries available through notice eviction and display clear, D-102 excludes failed-attempt transcripts and ends recovery on exit, and D-106 clears earlier recovery after a different successful turn. Test two failures with a newer third draft, count/order, both choices, focus, cancel, narrow layouts, view clearing and installed macOS/Linux UAT. D-108 retains confirmed selected entries until conversational success or D-109 confirmed dismissal; finite recovery-state limits are construction details; Chat/friday-cli behavior is unchanged.
independent_tui_product_decisions.confirmed_restore_pending_retention: D-108: after Confirm places a selected failed prompt into the editor, keep its exact submitted text/caret as the same pending current-run recovery entry. The chooser count/order and other entries do not change or duplicate; subsequent editor edits or replacement cannot mutate the original snapshot, and repeated Restore retrieves it again subject to D-41/D-101 Confirm/Cancel. Cancel changes neither editor nor pending set. A later successful conversational turn clears all earlier pending entries and Restore controls under D-106, whether it used a restored or different prompt; admission, partial output, failed turns, slash commands and display clearing do not. Restore makes no provider request or failed-attempt transcript record and does not alter active attachments. Test two pending failures, repeated Restore after edit/overwrite, count/order, Cancel, failed-versus-successful turn, disposable transcript, installed macOS/Linux UAT and unchanged Chat/friday-cli behavior. D-109 also permits confirmed per-prompt Dismiss; finite recovery-state limits are construction details.
independent_tui_product_decisions.failed_prompt_explicit_dismissal: D-109: offer Dismiss alongside singular Restore or on each entry in the multiple-prompt chooser. Confirm/Cancel protects removal of only the selected current-run recovery snapshot; Cancel preserves it. Confirm immediately updates count/order and singular-or-none controls, preserves the editor draft/caret including a restored copy and active attachments, and leaves any retained error notice non-actionable. Focus returns predictably. No provider call or failed-attempt transcript write. Test zero/one/two entries, keyboard/pointer access, Confirm/Cancel, focus, draft and attachment preservation, no provider/transcript effect and installed macOS/Linux UAT. Bind finite count/size and deterministic overflow behavior in the construction directive; no further failed-prompt product question is pending.
